results.question: Do I always need a prototype before certifying a BOM?
results.text: No. The prototype step is optional. A DRAFT or IN_REVIEW BOM can be certified directly for production when Prototype required is off. Prototype evidence is required only when Prototype required is on.

citations.title: Work order types, standalone production and optional prototype BOM certification

results.question: Can I create a production work order without a BOM?
results.text: No. A PRODUCTION work order, including a standalone one, can only be created, released, or started from a CERTIFIED BOM revision for the same part. TASK_ONLY and other non-production types are separate and do not bypass that requirement.

citations.title: Work order types, standalone production and optional prototype BOM certification

results.question: Does a standalone production WO still need a certified BOM?
results.text: Yes. A standalone production work order still requires a certified BOM for the same part. It does not require a sales order. Only CERTIFIED BOM revisions can be used to create, release, or start PRODUCTION work orders.

citations.title: Work order types, standalone production and optional prototype BOM certification

results.question: What if I need to change a certified BOM revision?
results.text: To change a certified or obsolete BOM, create a new revision. Certification locks the revision and obsoletes the previous certified revision, so the existing certified revision itself is not edited in place.

citations.title: Work order types, standalone production and optional prototype BOM certification

results.question: Which work order types are available?
results.text: Available work order types include PRODUCTION, TASK_ONLY, REWORK, INSPECTION, REPAIR, and PROTOTYPE. PRODUCTION work orders require a matching CERTIFIED BOM revision. The other types have their own rules and are not ways to bypass production certification.

citations.title: Work order types, standalone production and optional prototype BOM certification

results.question: How do I go from a quote to the customer PO to a sales order?
results.text: Start in Sales > Quotes, add a customer and quote lines, then send or revise the quote. When the customer accepts, record their purchase order number and convert the quote into a sales order in one step so pricing and lines flow onto the order. A customer PO is not your supplier purchase order. Review the resulting sales order; converting a quote does not by itself complete manufacturing or post cash.

citations.title: Quote to customer PO, sales order and work order

results.question: Is a customer PO the same as my supplier PO?
results.text: No. A customer PO is not your supplier purchase order. Record the customer's purchase order reference when converting a quote to a sales order; supplier purchase orders are created separately in purchasing.

results.text: Controlled Docs signatures bind to an exact revision and its content hash, using PIN verification. They record the signer and do not allow the assistant to sign, approve, or bypass a signature.

results.question: Why is starting a production WO blocked?
results.text: Starting a production work order is blocked unless that same part has a CERTIFIED BOM revision and the kit prerequisites are met. Production start checks both the certified BOM and kit readiness; inspect those blockers instead of forcing a status change. A standalone production WO still needs a certified BOM and does not bypass certification. If Prototype required is on, prototype evidence is required before the BOM can be certified for production.

citations.title: Work order types, standalone production and optional prototype BOM certification

results.question: Is completing a traveler step the same as completing the entire work order?
results.text: No. Completing one traveler step is different from completing the entire work order, and neither means a customer shipment or invoice has been completed.

results.question: How does receiving handle partial deliveries?
results.text: Receiving records supplier deliveries on receiving travelers and walks them through receipt, inspection, and putaway. A partial receipt stays separate from closing the purchase order, so the PO is not closed just because some of the delivery arrived.

citations.title: Purchase orders, receiving travelers and serialized stock

results.question: Are free text serial notes sufficient for serialized receiving?
results.text: No. Serialized items need the required individual serial records and quantities, not just a free-text serial note. Review quantities and serials if receiving or PO closure is blocked.

results.question: Where can I see as-built serial genealogy?

results.question: What is the difference between an NCR and a CAR?
results.text: An NCR records a nonconformance found in inspection or quality tracking and can escalate to MRB for material disposition. A CAR is a separate corrective-action record for root cause, corrective action, and verification so the problem does not recur. Creating a CAR does not by itself release held material.

results.question: Which module handles material review and disposition?
results.text: MRB handles material review and disposition. It sits with NCR/Quality and CAR in the quality workflow; use the required review and authorization steps before disposition.

results.question: Where do I manage customer returns and repairs?
results.text: Manage customer returns and repairs in RMA under Quality & Compliance at /rma. Each return authorization lets you receive the unit and route it to MRB or a repair work order, and it links back to the original order and serial.

results.question: Does using Protessera guarantee AS9100 certification?
results.text: No. Protessera supports compliance records, but using it does not guarantee AS9100, CMMC, or DCAA certification.

results.question: Where do products, requirements and configuration changes live?
results.text: Products live in the PLM product catalog, which links each product’s BOM, work instructions, procedures, and program. Requirements are tracked in Requirements, including verification coverage. Configuration changes are handled in Config Management: propose them as ECR submissions, then release them so the document is revised and the prior master is archived.

results.question: What do SPI and CPI mean in PMO?
results.text: In PMO earned value, SPI is earned value divided by planned value, and CPI is earned value divided by actual cost. They show schedule and cost performance at a glance. The figures depend on the underlying records and do not certify financial accuracy.

results.question: What are direct and indirect budget charge codes?
results.text: Budgets define direct or indirect charge codes and enacted budget authority. Forecast work is direct job cost; standalone budgets are company indirect. The charge-code owner approves time and material against the budget, which is where PRs and timesheets hit a budget. Values depend on underlying records and do not certify financial accuracy. Review program policy and budget approval before spending; the assistant cannot enact a budget.

results.question: What should I do when an AR/AP posting fails?
results.text: If an AR/AP posting fails, capture the record reference and contact human support from the Support tab. Do not create a manual duplicate journal to hide the failed posting.

results.question: Does accounting automatically file my payroll taxes?
results.text: No. Do not treat payroll tax filing as automatic just because payroll screens exist.
